title: ר' שמעון בן לקיש
author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness

paragraphs: 1. R' Yohanan's brother-in-law. R' Yohanan was bathing in the Jordan. Resh Lakish saw him and leaped into the Jordan after him. He said, “Your strength is for Torah!” He answered, “Your beauty is for women!” He said, “If you turn back, I shall give you my sister, who is more beautiful than I”: Bava Metzia 84a; see there at length.

2. R' Yohanan's pupil-colleague. In Gittin, chapter 2, 19a, Resh Lakish said to R' Yohanan, “Our teacher, you taught us.” In Hullin 139a: this was before he heard from his teacher R' Yohanan. In Ta'anit 8a: he arranged his teaching forty times, corresponding to the forty days in which the Torah was given, and went before R' Yohanan. In Berakhot 31a: he did not fill his mouth with laughter after hearing from his teacher R' Yohanan that it is forbidden to fill one's mouth with laughter in this world. R' Yohanan said of Resh Lakish, “My counterpart disagrees with me”: Rashi explains, equal to me, Ketubbot 84b. On 54b he explains, a man of my stature, fit to disagree with me. In Hullin 18b, Resh Lakish permitted slaughter with the edge of a helmet. R' Yohanan called out to him, “Gisa, gisa!” Rashi explains, “You were excessive, excessive”—that is, you permitted too much. End of quotation. It seems to me that because he was married to R' Yohanan's sister, he called him “My brother-in-law, my brother-in-law,” a play on words: my brother-in-law, you permitted too much, meaning excessive. Afterward I found that Torat Hayyim, Zeh Borer, and Nimukei Yosef write likewise, and it pleased me. Ha-Ma'or writes likewise there, and responsa Mabit, no. 313. In Me'ilah 7b, R' Yohanan said, “I have cut off the youngster's legs,” meaning Resh Lakish. Rashi explains: he calls Resh Lakish a youngster because he was younger than he; he objected to him and he could not answer. He asked R' Yohanan: Beitzah 19b. Resh Lakish objected to R' Yohanan: Sukkah 46b. R' Yohanan objected to Resh Lakish: Pesahim 34a, 84b; Sukkah 46b; Bava Metzia 90, end of side b. R' Yohanan said in Resh Lakish's name: Shabbat 15b. R' Yohanan said to Resh Lakish, “But from where does the master derive it?”: Yoma 3, end of side b. In Hullin 75b and Shevuot 40a, 45b, he would wait silently. Rashi: this was Resh Lakish's manner when R' Yohanan said something; he waited to answer until R' Yohanan had finished all he needed, and afterward disputed him. Some say Resh Lakish was drinking water when R' Yohanan said that teaching. In Hullin, Rashi explains that Resh Lakish waited before disputing him, perhaps he would retract. See Ketubbot 104b; Nedarim 77a; Arukh, entries Shanah and Shatak.

He told R' Yohanan, “What benefit have you brought me? There they called me master, here they call me master ….” R' Yohanan was distressed. Resh Lakish fell ill, and his wife, R' Yohanan's sister, came so that he would pray for him, but he did not wish to, and Resh Lakish died. R' Yohanan was distressed because he could not find a pupil like him. The rabbis said, “Let R' Elazar ben Pedat go, for his teachings are sharp.” To everything R' Yohanan said, R' Elazar said, “A teaching supports you.” R' Yohanan said, “Are you like bar Lakisha? He raised twenty-four objections to everything, and I gave twenty-four resolutions.” R' Yohanan wept, saying, “Where is bar Lakisha?” He cried out until his mind slipped away. The rabbis sought mercy, and R' Yohanan died: Bava Metzia 84, end of side a. Resh Lakish died one year before R' Yohanan: Sefer Keritut. After Resh Lakish's death, his child studied before R' Yohanan. His mother removed him so that he would not set his eyes on him, since he was wise. He asked him, “What does ‘You shall surely tithe’ mean …?”: Ta'anit, first chapter, 9a.

3. Tosafot write in Bava Metzia, Ha-Po'alim, 84—Shalshelet ha-Kabbalah writes Eizehu Neshekh, which is a scribal error—that Resh Lakish knew much before studying with R' Yohanan, but cast off Torah's yoke, became an ignoramus, and engaged in banditry. Tosafot, Eruvin 65b, write likewise. Resh Lakish and R' Hanina's pupils came to an inn, where the renter was absent and the lessor was present, and so forth. Resh Lakish said, “Let us rent; when we reach our teachers in the South we shall ask them.” They came and asked R' Efes, who said, “You acted properly,” and so forth. Tosafot write: this proves Rabbenu Tam's view that Resh Lakish was already a great man before coming before R' Yohanan, for this event was near Rabbi's death, since they asked R' Efes, who lived only two and a half years after Rabbi; see his entry. This is also implied in Tosafot, Yevamot 57a, s.v. Ata: here it implies that Resh Lakish was great when he came before R' Yohanan, for he studied Torah before R' Hoshaya, R' Yohanan's teacher. See below, where Resh Lakish often reports in R' Hoshaya's name.

4. In Gittin 47a he sold himself to the Ludim, and used to say, “My belly is my cushion.” Tosafot write that they used to lie on their bellies, as in Zevahim 5, beginning of side a: Resh Lakish lay on his belly in the study hall and raised an objection. A gloss in Ein Yaakov there says that this is good for digestion, as written in צ״ל [unresolved bibliographic initials; Tz.L.], rule 3, chapter 9. In Sanhedrin 24a, Ulla said that seeing Resh Lakish in the study hall is like seeing him uproot mountains and grind them against one another. In Yoma 9, end of side b, he did not speak with Rabbah bar bar Hana. Whoever Resh Lakish spoke with in the marketplace was given business without witnesses. He did not even speak with R' Elazar, master of the Land of Israel. Tosafot explain that he did not begin speaking with him, but when R' Elazar began, he answered; proof is Zevahim 5, where he answered him. Tosafot Yeshanim there: he did not initiate any joking conversation with him. Yet in Ketubbot, chapter 2, 25b, we find him speaking with him: “Have you heard bar Nappaha's words?” Perhaps he did not speak in the marketplace. Resh Lakish went to greet Rabbi, who said, “Pray for me”: Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 78. This too proves that Resh Lakish was a great man before coming before R' Yohanan, since Rabbi said, “Pray for me.” Maginnei Shelomoh, Pesahim 69b, labored to prove that Resh Lakish lived in the tannaim's days; he did not see this midrash, which places him in Rabbi's days, and Rabbi was a tanna.

In Jerusalem Berakhot: he went beyond the Shabbat boundary because of his study. In Berakhot 44a: he ate Ginnosar fruit until his mind became disordered, and R' Yehudah Nesiah would send people to bring him home. In Shabbat 119, end of side b, Resh Lakish reports two things in R' Yehudah Nesiah's name, and told R' Yehudah Nesiah, “Thus I have received from my forebears”; some say, from your forebears. In Mo'ed Katan 17a, Resh Lakish excommunicated a man who ate figs, saying, “Let this man be under a ban.” He said to him, and so forth, “If I have become financially liable to you ….” They went to the study hall, where they said, “His ban is a ban; yours is not.” He said, “May I be the atonement of R' Hiyya and his sons”: Sukkah 20, end of side a. Rashi: an expression of honor when mentioning one's father or teacher after his death.

5. Resh Lakish was Mordekhai. Because he provoked Haman and caused an entire nation to be taken for slaughter, he sold himself to the Ludim to atone for himself. He is Shaul ben Kish, and this one ben Lakish. He sold himself to the Ludim as Shaul sold himself to death by the Philistines, to fall into their hands; he did so to take vengeance on them. This is “Lest the daughters of the uncircumcised rejoice.” Resh Lakish told the Ludim, “Are you laughing at me?” We find: Shaul with one, and it did not avail him; David with two, and it availed him. This is a scribal error: it should read, “Shaul with one, and it counted against him”—Rashi: for harm, punishing him with death and the abolition of his kingdom—whereas David failed in two and neither counted against him: Yoma 22. Thus Shaul was punished for one. Therefore Resh Lakish said in Sanhedrin 111, “‘It opened its mouth without measure’—even one who left one statute,” as happened to him. He effected the tikkun of Tuval Kayin, “the sharpener of every worker in copper and iron,” because Resh Lakish was a chief of outlaws and a killer of people. This is alluded to in Bava Metzia 84a: “A sword and a knife—from when do they receive impurity?” R' Yohanan said to Resh Lakish, “A bandit knows his banditry,” meaning he was expert in his former craft, sharpening: Sefer Gilgulei Neshamot; see its end. He was a reincarnation of Yishmael, hence “A bandit knows his banditry”: לקונטי מהר״ש מגיד [provisionally Likkutei Maharash Maggid].

6. Regarding the halakhic ruling against R' Yohanan, see his entry. The halakhah follows Resh Lakish in three: Yevamot 36a; Bava Batra 129b; Hullin 29b, Tosafot, that a statement in Levi the Elder's name is not included. See Tosafot, Shabbat 70b. עכ״ש [unresolved bibliographic initials; E.K.Sh.] writes concerning Terumot, chapter 8: a group met gentiles who said, “Give us one of you to kill; otherwise we shall kill you all.” They must not hand over one person. If they singled out someone, like Sheva ben Bikhri, they should hand him over rather than be killed. Resh Lakish said that this applies only when he is liable to death like Sheva ben Bikhri; R' Yohanan said even if he is not liable to death. Beit Yosef, Yoreh De'ah, no. 157, wondered why Rambam rules like Resh Lakish rather than R' Yohanan, whom the halakhah follows against Resh Lakish. It is no difficulty, because R' Akiva and Ben Peturi hold like Resh Lakish. End of quotation. See there: R' Akiva holds that your life takes precedence. Thus Resh Lakish's position, that when there is no death liability they should all die, is not R' Akiva's. Ben Peturi, however, holds like Resh Lakish, that all should die. It is difficult how he ruled like Ben Peturi against R' Akiva.

7. R' Abba said in Resh Lakish's name. R' Abba bar Zavda. R' Abba bar Kahana. In Abba Kohen Bardela's name. He explained Avdimi bar ha-Madori's words. R' Avahu said in Resh Lakish's name. Abaye said several things in Resh Lakish's name: Shabbat 63a. R' Avin said in Resh Lakish's name. Avin of Tzippori. R' Avin bar Hiyya. R' Avdimi of Haifa. In R' Hoshaya's name: Kiddushin 80a; Niddah 18b; Bekhorot 13a. Tosafot, Yevamot 57a, write that he was Resh Lakish's teacher. Ayvu. R' Illa. R' Ila said: Resh Lakish said, “R' Meir used to say.” In R' Elazar ben Azaryah's name: Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 9. R' Elazar said in Resh Lakish's name, in R' Yehudah bar Hanina's name. Resh Lakish was annoyed with him because he did not report the teaching in his name in the study hall. Resh Lakish showed him a dinar; see his entry. R' Elazar ben Mallui. R' Ammi. R' Assi. He asked R' Efes; see above. R' Ephraim the scribe. Rav Ashi reports in his name. Rav Bibi. R' Berekhiah and R' Yonah, in R' Yehudah the Nasi's name: Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 98. R' Gurion. Rav Huna bar Ketina said to him. R' Hila. Rabbi Vestina was his pupil. R' Zeira. R' Ze'ira in Hizkiyah's name. Resh Lakish cried out—Rashi: shouted loudly—to the elders of the South. R' Hizkiyah in R' Hiyya's name. He fasted three hundred fasts to see R' Hiyya the Great after his death; see his entry. R' Hiyya bar Ashi said in Resh Lakish's name. R' Hiyya bar Abba said; see his entry. R' Hiyya bar Adda taught Scripture or Mishnah to Resh Lakish's sons. R' Hiyya bar Adda, Bar Kappara's sister's son: all one person. R' Hiyya bar Yosef answered him. With R' Hiyya bar Zarnuki. Halfaya. R' Hama bar Ukva. He asked R' Hanina: Shabbat 114a. Eruvin 80a; Avodah Zarah 11, end of side b, in a great man's name—who? R' Hanina. And R' Hanina bar Pappa. R' Hanina of Anatot. R' Hanan, אבוי [his father; referent unresolved]. R' Hananyah. R' Tovyana.

In R' Yehudah bar Hanina's name; see above. In R' Yehudah the Nasi's name; see above. In R' Yehudah Nesiah's name, and before R' Yehudah Nesiah; see his entry. R' Yehudah ben Pazi disagrees with him. R' Yehudah bar Nahman. R' Yudan bar Nehemyah. R' Yehudah bar Immi. R' Yehoshua ben Levi reports in his name: Makkot 2a. In R' Yehoshua's name: Midrash Eikhah, at “From the daughter of Zion went out.” R' Yohanan was his teacher. R' Yohanan said in Resh Lakish's name; see above. R' Yusta. R' Yustina: the foregoing Vestina. In R' Yose bar Hanina's name. He eulogized R' Yose of Mimalhaya. Yose bar Ashyan. Rav Yosef said in R' Shimon ben Lakish's name: Shabbat 94a. In R' Yannai's name. R' Yannai son of R' Yishmael. R' Yaakov bar Idi. R' Yaakov bar Adda was in his time. R' Yaakov of Kefar Hanan. R' Yaakov bar Immi reports in his name. He said, “R' Yitzhak Nappaha is better than bar Nappaha”—R' Yohanan; see his entry. R' Yitzhak said in Resh Lakish's name. R' Yitzhak bar Nahmani. R' Yitzhak bar Ostaya. With R' Yitzhak Pasaka. R' Yitzhak bar Maryon. R' Yitzhak Ruba. R' Yirmeyah said in Resh Lakish's name: Yoma 80b; Makkot 17a; Zevahim 22a; Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Keitzad Mevarekhin; Shabbat 93a. R' Yirmeyah bar Abba said in Resh Lakish's name. R' Yishmael bar Abba. R' Yishmael ben Zirz. Rav Kahana said in Resh Lakish's name. In Levi the Elder's name. R' Levi bar Hama said in Resh Lakish's name. R' Mallai was in his time. And R' Mani bar Pattish. In R' Sovaya's name. R' Suma bar Ketavat. R' Simon. R' Samya said. Ulla reports in his name. Akavyah asked him. Rav Ketina. Bar Kappara: see below. Rava bar Ittai said to him. Rabbah bar Ahoti said to him. Rabbah bar bar Hana. Ravin. Rami bar Hama reports in his name. R' Shalmoni reports in his name. In R' Shimon bar Kahana's name. R' Shimon bar Abba said. In R' Shimon ben Menasya's name. In R' Shimon bar Kappara's name: Pesahim 15a; Ta'anit 8, end of side a; Bava Metzia 26a; Jerusalem Terumot 7:3; Hagigah 23b; Bereshit Rabbah, chapters 41, 42. He called R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak a cattle herder. R' Shimon ben Kisma. R' Shimon bar Narshaya. R' Shimon ben Elyakim asked him. R' Shimon ben Yasinai. In Bar Tutni's name. In Te'oni's name. R' Tanhum.
